name: Fortunate Isles

attributes.attribute: islands off the coasts of Ireland and Scotland
home of fairies or the Tuatha De Danann

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Fortunate Isles form a mythological site. Islands near the coasts of Ireland and Scotland take this name. The name reports a belief that the gods or the fairies dwelled on lovely islands that ride the open western sea.

okr.objective: The Fortunate Isles are the floating islands of the western sea.
key_results: The Fortunate Isles are a mythological site.
The name fits islands off Ireland and Scotland.
Fairies or the gods lived there.
The isles float in the western sea.
